reading: The multi-coloured block at the left edge is copied flush against the right edge, and each row's gap between the two copies is filled with that row's edge colour (the block's first and last columns share a colour).
verb: copy to far edge and bridge
why: output = block at left, block at right edge, and every row's middle cells equal the colour of the block cells bounding them

reading: Each solid 8 rectangle is recoloured by quadrant: top-left 6, top-right 1, bottom-left 2, bottom-right 3, and its core (cells at least 2 in from the rectangle's edge) becomes 4.

slots.subject: each solid colour-8 rectangle (even sides)
slots.quadrant colours: TL 6, TR 1, BL 2, BR 3 (split at the half-height and half-width)
slots.core: cells at distance >= 2 from the rectangle's border -> 4

why: every 8 cell is recoloured by its quadrant or core position; background unchanged

reading: Two opposite grid edges are full lines of different colours; next to every colour-1 cell one cell is painted on the side facing the nearer edge line, in that line's colour.

slots.subject: each colour-1 single cell
slots.borders: the two opposite full edge lines (rows or columns) with their colours
slots.mark: the orthogonal neighbour of the cell in the direction of the nearer border line, coloured as that line

why: each 1 cell gets exactly one new neighbour, toward the closer coloured edge, with that edge's colour

reading: Every object slides right by exactly its own width (bounding-box width).

new_rows.name: width_shift
new_rows.datalog:
xlo(O, min(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
xhi(O, max(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
wid(O, W) :- xlo(O, A), xhi(O, B), D = B - A, W = D + 1.
width_shift(Y, X2) :- obj(O, Y, X), wid(O, W), X2 = X + W.

why: each object keeps its shape and its new left edge is at old left + width (it lands just right of where it was)

reading: The noisy grid hides several partial octagon rings (6x6 ring shape) of distinct colours; the output stacks one clean copy of the ring per colour vertically on the background, ordered by their position in the input.

slots.colours: the colours of the partial rings found in the input, ordered along their diagonal/left-to-right position
slots.layout: 6 wide, 6 rows per ring, stacked top to bottom

why: output height = 6 x number of ring colours; each 6x6 block is the ring template in one ring colour

reading: The 2x2 block in the centre of the 4x4 grid is pushed apart: each of its cells moves to the grid corner on its side.

slots.subject: the four cells of the central 2x2 block
slots.target: the grid corner nearest each cell (TL->TL, TR->TR, BL->BL, BR->BR)

why: each block cell's colour appears at the corresponding grid corner; all else background

reading: Colour-3 cells that belong to an orthogonally connected group of 2 or more become 8; lone 3 cells (no orthogonal 3 neighbour) stay 3.

new_rows.name: paired
new_rows.datalog:
paired(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DY = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).
paired(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).

why: every 3 cell with an orthogonal 3 neighbour becomes 8 (key 3->8); nothing else changes

reading: A full vertical line crosses a full horizontal line; the 8 cells around the crossing are painted 4, the crossing cell keeps its colour.

new_rows.name: cross_ring
new_rows.datalog:
rn(Y, count(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rf(Y, count(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
fullrow(Y) :- rn(Y, N), rf(Y, M), N = M.
cn(X, count(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
cf(X, count(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
fullcol(X) :- cn(X, N), cf(X, M), N = M.
cross_ring(Y2, X2) :- fullrow(Y), fullcol(X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX.

why: the 8 neighbours of the full-row/full-column intersection are colour 4; nothing else changes

reading: Two 3x3 colour-2 boxes with a 5 centre each have one missing edge cell (a door); the door cells and a rectangular corridor of 4 joining the two doors' outsides are filled, leaving the area behind each box (the side opposite its door) empty.

slots.subject: two 3x3 boxes, each with one gap cell (door) in an edge middle
slots.region: the rectangle spanned by the two cells just outside the doors, minus the boxes and minus each box's row/column band on the side opposite its door; plus both door cells

why: all filled cells are 4, lie in that corridor, and the boxes are untouched

reading: From the 2 cell on the bottom row a two-cell-thick staircase of 2s climbs up-right to the top/right edge; when its next cell is a 1, the staircase shifts right past the 1s (widening the row below) and continues.

slots.source: the single colour-2 cell on the bottom row
slots.direction: up-right diagonal, each row two cells wide (cols c and c+1 when the row above starts at c+1)
slots.obstacles: colour-1 cells; on collision the path shifts right until clear, the lower row is extended to stay connected

why: every row above the source holds a contiguous run of 2s continuing the diagonal, never overwriting 1s
